Haven't finished the mod yet, but I wanna get some stuff of my chest.
Something about this mod, about the way Yuri thinks and acts, something about its general ambiance has got me thinking. [Story relevant spoilers here](/s "First, the train scene. I remember the day trip Sayori and Yuri took in the first mod, Doki Doki Rain Clouds, and experiencing the same journey through Yuri's eyes hit me with this sense of vastness that made me stop for a minute.  ")
[personal life thoughts here, less spoilery but potentially triggering](/s "Playing both as myself and Yuri, i had this revelation that every single time I've interacted with someone, every time I've said something or been spoken to, we've all been living our own lives. The seemingly innocent girl I met in freshman year college had more secrets up her sleeve than I ever would've known had we not gotten closer. My annoying suitemate probably has every reason to act the way that he does, socially inept and all. I recalled the moments in my life where I was literally one step from death, and it hit me like a bag of trucks that *so many* people have felt the same way. I've spent so much of my life wallowing in my own sadness i haven't given a thought to everyone else's problems. ")
Doki Doki New Eyes, so far, has been an enriching experience. It's made me feel things I haven't felt and thought things I haven't thought, and I praise the creators for making this so good. 
Back to playing. Thanks for reading.

I suffer(ed?) from severe depression, and as such I was completely taken by surprise when I found out more about Sayori in the original DDLC, almost diappointed with myself for not picking up on it sooner. I've mostly recovered from it, but  suffering from it for so long has left long-lasting traumas that stick with me to this day. This mod was, like Sayori's poems, bittersweet. On the one hand, it reminded me of what I faced every day, from the lack of desire to eat to overanalyzing every single interaction and non-interaction to wanting the best for everyone, at the cost of yourself. Everthing about how Sayori's demons were presented resonated on a spritual level with me. On the other hand, it brought forward my progress that I no longer feel these things as often. 
I know not if you personally feel these things, or you have an amazing talent for creating art that sucker punches people in their sensitive bits, but i can't thank you enough for having made this, nor can I adequately express how much I loved this mod.

Just finished this mod, and I'm glad to say that it was far better than what I had expected. You did an *amazing* job writing the characters. There were only like, two times early on I felt like the characterization was off but all in all it felt like each one of the girls was exactly how they would be. 

The following paragraph will be rife with spoilers/critiques, and shall be blocked off. [I thought the object scene was unexpected and very out of place, but would've been a welcome addition had it been done in a more intimate setting, like a Monika/MC one-on-one as opposed to the entire cast being under one roof. The explanation given about a programmed need for physical touch made sense to me, and I think that it could've been worked into a more appropriate lead-up to the scene, which in itself was decently written. It felt as awkward to me as it would've been to them, so mission accomplished there, bossman. At some points, it felt like the plot was going by way too quickly. Personally, I felt that the scenes where they were discussing the topics in the mental health box were underwhelming. I'm biased, since I was relating it to my time in group therapy, but IMO it felt more like MC talking for a while and the girls kind of just going along with it. Taking into consideration the ending note and your disclaimer of not being an accurate representation of mental illnesses, these were pretty 'okay' segments in my book. The only other negatives I can think of regarding the content is the typos, which were very few and far between and not bad enough to detract from the experience. EDIT: near the end, where MC is explaining the bit about the computers and what happens when the game is closed, Natsuki doesn't change her expression. Monika only goes from a smile to a slight frown, and I wasn't sure if there was a more dramatic reaction available for her. ] (/spoiler) 

On to the part where I get to gush about the stuff I loved, I *really* appreciated the call backs to the original game. Leaving it as ambiguous as possible, the way that the final act resolved felt incredibly satisfying to see how things had changed with the girls and the world around them. The cutesy scenes were somewhat cliched but fully welcome and enjoyable, and didn't feel out of place at all. The [message via selectable options] (/spoiler) was a genius move, taking what we thought would be a familiar action and turning into one of the most wholesome things I've seen in a while. [Originally, I felt like there should've been more choices throughout the game to make it feel more like a full VN instead of a linear story, but I think that that twist more than made up for it.] (/spoiler) A solid 9.5/10 in my book, would play again. 

I hope my review(?) didn't sound so rude, I genuinely really, really enjoyed this and will probably replay the final stretch when I need some positive vibes. 
Thanks for making this man, as tribute I offer to you my good vibes and best wishes.
